The built-in application

Muhammad Yaseen

2026-11-05

Source: vignettes/bayesammi_12_app.qmd

\[ \newcommand{\vy}{\mathbf{y}} \newcommand{\vx}{\mathbf{x}} \newcommand{\vb}{\mathbf{b}} \newcommand{\ve}{\mathbf{e}} \newcommand{\vone}{\mathbf{1}} \newcommand{\vbeta}{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \newcommand{\vmu}{\boldsymbol{\mu}} \newcommand{\mX}{\mathbf{X}} \newcommand{\mZ}{\mathbf{Z}} \newcommand{\mV}{\mathbf{V}} \newcommand{\mI}{\mathbf{I}} \newcommand{\mJ}{\mathbf{J}} \newcommand{\mSigma}{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} \newcommand{\mY}{\mathbf{Y}} \newcommand{\mK}{\mathbf{K}} \newcommand{\mH}{\mathbf{H}} \newcommand{\va}{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \newcommand{\vg}{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \newcommand{\vt}{\boldsymbol{\tau}} \newcommand{\vd}{\boldsymbol{\delta}} \newcommand{\vtheta}{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \newcommand{\vv}{\mathbf{v}} \newcommand{\E}{\mathrm{E}} \newcommand{\Var}{\mathrm{Var}} \newcommand{\Cov}{\mathrm{Cov}} \newcommand{\tr}{\operatorname{tr}} \]

1 Abstract

bam_app() opens an application in the web browser that runs every analysis of the package without code. This vignette describes its pages and how it keeps its results reproducible.

2 Starting the application 

bam_app(
    launch.browser = TRUE
  )

The application needs the suggested packages shiny, bslib and DT. magick with WebP support is optional: with it the plots are sent to the browser as lossless WebP images, about half the size of the same PNG.

isTRUE(tryCatch(requireNamespace("magick", quietly = TRUE) && isTRUE(magick::magick_config()$webp),
                error = function(e) FALSE))
[1] TRUE

TRUE means WebP is available. A magick installation that no longer loads, because the ImageMagick libraries of the system were removed or upgraded, gives FALSE, and the application then sends PNG images; reinstalling magick restores WebP.

3 The pages

Page What it does
Home what the application does and the order of the pages
Data the Maiz example or a CSV file with one row per plot; choice of the response, genotype, environment and replicate columns
Model AMMI or GGE, number of terms, common or environment-specific variances, iterations, burn-in, thinning, chains, seed and priors; then the summary, traces and densities
Biplot the biplot with HPD regions, for genotypes, environments or both
Decisions winners, probabilities of superior performance, ranks, stability and predictions
Stability Bayesian Eberhart-Russell, Finlay-Wilkinson and Shukla models; classical and AMMI-based stability indices
Model choice posterior predictive checks and a comparison of the fits of the session

Every result page has the same tabs:

  • Interpretation gives the plain-language reading of bam_interpret(), with a button that copies it, and the sources of the method.
  • Plot shows the figure, which can be saved as PNG, PDF or WebP.
  • Table shows the numbers, rounded, in a sortable table with buttons to copy them or save them as CSV or Excel.
  • Output shows the printed result as text, with a button that copies it.

The model page has a further tab, R code, with the code that reproduces the fit outside the application.

The model page after a fit, with the interpretation tab open:

The plot tab of the Bayesian Eberhart-Russell model on the Stability menu:

The screenshots are lossless WebP in the HTML version: 62 KB for the first, against 147 KB for the lossy JPEG of the PDF version.

4 Reproducibility

For the default settings with environment-specific variances, the R code tab shows:

settings <-
  list(
      .y      = "y"
    , .gen    = "entry"
    , .env    = "site"
    , .rep    = "rep"
    , .nIter  = 3000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 2
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 1
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = TRUE
    )
cat(bayesammi:::.bam_app_code(a = settings, source = "maiz"))
library(bayesammi)
data(Maiz)
fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 3000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 2
    , .priors = bam_priors(lambda_var = 1e+08, nu = 1)
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 1
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = TRUE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
fit
bam_interpret(
    x             = fit
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , top           = 5
  )

The seed fixes the draws, so the code returns the same numbers as the application.

5 Deploying

bam_app_object() returns the application object without running it, for a server:

# app.R on a Shiny server
bayesammi::bam_app_object()

Crossa, J., Perez-Elizalde, S., Jarquin, D., Cotes, J. M., Viele, K., Liu, G. and Cornelius, P. L. (2011). Bayesian estimation of the additive main effects and multiplicative interaction model. Crop Science, 51(4), 1458–1469. doi:10.2135/cropsci2010.06.0343
